task: My college roommate Kelsey is getting married in Charleston in June and I just found out I can't go because of a work commitment that I can't move. Write a text reply to her saying I'm devastated to miss it, I'll send a gift, and I'd love a video of the reception.
rewrite:
ambition:     A close friend would put the regret first and the logistics second, and would name something specific to ask for, like the first dance or the toasts, instead of a vague "send me a video." She would also keep the reason for missing it to one clause so it doesn't read as an excuse.
agency:       The raw material is Kelsey's own message announcing the wedding or sending the invite, which shows how she writes and how excited she is. It's in the user's text thread. It isn't available here, so assume a warm, casual, close-friend register.
acceleration: Use the regret-then-reason-then-gift-then-ask order, with the gift sentence sounding like a promise rather than an afterthought. Keep it to text-message length and mirror Kelsey's register, whether that means exclamation points, a nickname, or an emoji.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the user can check this. The closest proxy is the user reading it next to Kelsey's own message to see whether it sounds like something they'd actually send her. Her reply is the only real test.

deeper task:
Write a text message from me to my college roommate Kelsey, replying to her news that she's getting married in Charleston in June. I just found out I can't make it because of a work commitment I can't move. Say that I'm devastated to miss it, that I'll send a gift, and that I'd love a video of the reception. Make it sound like a close friend texting: lead with how much I wish I could be there, give the work reason in a few words, make the gift a real promise, and ask for a specific video moment, like the first dance or the toasts, instead of a generic "send me a video." Keep it short enough for a text, with no stiff phrasing, and don't invent any shared memories or details I haven't given you.

answers.plain:
Here's a draft you can send:

"Kelsey, I'm so sorry, but I just found out I can't make it to the wedding. I have a work commitment I can't move, and I'm absolutely devastated. I was so looking forward to celebrating you in Charleston. I'll be sending a gift, and I'd love a video of the reception if anyone can take one. I'll be there in spirit, and I can't wait to hear all about it. Love you tons!"

I can make it shorter, funnier, or more formal if you'd like.
answers.nudge:
**Main version**

> Kelsey!! First of all, I'm so happy for you both. I just found out I can't make it to the wedding because of a work commitment I can't move, and I'm genuinely devastated. I've been looking forward to seeing you walk down that aisle, and I hate that I'll miss it.
>
> I'll be sending a gift your way, and I'll be there in spirit the whole day. One request: I'd love a video of the reception, even a few clips of the dancing and toasts. I want to see everything!
>
> Can we plan a dinner soon after, so I can hear all about it and celebrate properly? Love you tons. ❤️

**Shorter version**

> Kelsey, I'm so sorry, I can't make it to the wedding. A work commitment came up that I can't move, and I'm devastated to miss it. I'm sending you a gift and I'll be cheering you on from afar. Would you (or someone in the wedding party) send me a video of the reception? I want to see all of it. Love you both so much! ❤️

**Tips**
- **Send it soon.** Telling her early is kinder, and she'll still be finalizing headcounts.
- **Add something personal if you can.** One line like "remember when we swore we'd be each other's bridesmaids?" will mean more than any polish.
- **Ask for the video lightly.** She'll be busy that day, so it may land better as "whenever someone gets a chance" than as a task for her. A friend or the videographer can send it later.
- **Follow through on the gift.** Order it from the registry now so it arrives around the wedding. A handwritten card makes up for some of the distance.

I can make it funnier, more emotional, or more casual, or tailor it to your friendship if you give me a detail or two.
